radar.title: Robustness-led and stability-responsive rescheduling: A Stackelberg game-theoretic formulation
radar.summary: Scheduling under disruptions poses a fundamental challenge in operations research, as decision makers must hierarchically prioritize system robustness while responding with schedule stability in real time. Existing rescheduling approaches typically rely on symmetric or weighted formulations, which obscure the leader-follower decision asymmetry inherent in disruption management and fail to provide a principled coordination mechanism between robustness and stability. This study formulates disrupted rescheduling as a hierarchical decision-making problem and proposes a Stackelberg game-theoretic formulation grounded in bilevel optimization. The structure explicitly models robustness as the Leader’s strategic objective and stability as the Follower’s responsive objective, thereby capturing the endogenous priority structure observed in practical rescheduling decisions. A baseline schedule is first constructed via multi-objective optimization to define the feasible and performance-relevant region for subsequent adjustments. Under disruptions, rescheduling decisions are then derived through backward induction by characterizing the subgame-perfect Nash equilibrium (SPNE) of the Stackelberg game, yielding sequential and priority-aware responses that coordinate stability within robustness-led constraints. Computational experiments on standard benchmark instances demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves a robustness-stability coordination unattainable by conventional strategies. In particular, the Stackelberg-based model attains robustness levels statistically indistinguishable from robustness-dominant complete rescheduling, while simultaneously improving schedule stability by an average of 39.52% relative to stability-oriented right-shift rescheduling. These results indicate that explicitly modeling rescheduling as a hierarchical bilevel game enables superior performance continuity under disruptions. The study contributes to the literature by introducing a decision-theoretic perspective on rescheduling under disruptions, establishing Stackelberg games as a unifying framework for robustness-stability coordination, and offering a transferable modeling paradigm for complex scheduling problems with hierarchical priorities.

radar.title: Challenges and Opportunities in Records and Archives Management of the Legislative Departments in the Province of Antique: Basis for a Proposed Digitized Data Banking System
radar.venue_raw: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
radar.summary: This study determined the challenges and opportunities in records and archives management in the legislative departments of the 18 municipalities in the Province of Antique as a basis for a proposed digitized data banking system. A descriptive-quantitative design was employed using total enumeration of 18 records officers directly responsible for legislative records and archives. Data were gathered through a validated researcher-made questionnaire, pilot-tested for reliability, and analyzed using percentages and weighted means in IBM SPSS Statistics. Findings showed that the extent of implementation was weakest in data acquisition (M = 3.22), while data storage (M = 4.00) and data security (M = 3.94) were generally implemented but remained constrained by limited server capacity, environmental risks, absence of encryption, and insufficient cybersecurity training. The principal challenges were data acquisition (M = 3.53), data storage (M = 3.43), and data security (M = 3.86), with recurring concerns involving insufficient ICT infrastructure, financial limitations, staff capability gaps, and weak protection mechanisms. Respondents strongly supported opportunities for improvement in data acquisition (M = 4.47), data storage (M = 4.21), and data security (M = 4.31), particularly through ICT investment, standardized digital procedures, regular backups, scalable cloud systems, advanced cybersecurity measures, and staff training. The study concluded that legislative departments recognize the weaknesses of current records practices and demonstrate readiness for technological and procedural modernization. A phased digitized data banking system integrating digital acquisition, cloud-based storage, encryption, access controls, standardized procedures, and capacity-building was therefore proposed to strengthen efficiency, accessibility, accountability, and records security.

radar.title: E-Banking Administration and Customer Satisfaction in Nigerian Deposit Money Banks: Evidence from ATM, Internet and Mobile Banking Services
radar.venue_raw: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
radar.summary: The rapid expansion of digital banking has fundamentally changed how money banks deposit financial services and engage with their customers. However, despite the growing use of electronic banking channels in Nigeria, customers still encounter difficulties such as unsuccessful transactions, network interruptions, cybersecurity concerns, and inadequate or delayed responses to complaints. This study investigated the effect of e-banking administration on customer satisfaction among selected deposit money banks in Nigeria, focusing specifically on Automated Teller Machine (ATM), internet banking, and mobile banking services. A descriptive survey design was employed, and primary data was obtained through structured questionnaires administered to bank customers. From the 120 questionnaires distributed, 110 were properly completed and retrieved, yielding a response rate of 91.7%. The collected data were examined using descriptive statistics and regression analysis. The results demonstrated that ATM services had a statistically significant effect on customer satisfaction (R² = .610, β = .742, p < .001). Similarly, internet banking recorded a significant positive effect on customer satisfaction (R² = .646, β = .782, p < .001), while mobile banking also showed a significant positive relationship with customer satisfaction (R² = .676, β = .801, p < .001). Descriptive findings indicated generally favourable customer assessments of the three electronic banking channels, reflected in grand mean scores of 4.09 for ATM services, 4.15 for internet banking, and 4.13 for mobile banking. The study concludes that efficient management of electronic banking services contributes significantly to enhanced customer satisfaction. It therefore recommends sustained investment in technological reliability, cybersecurity measures, user-friendly platforms, transaction monitoring systems, and efficient mechanisms for resolving customer complaints.
